assign.outcome:
**A bled grid or flex wall now pays its gutter back everywhere, not just on `previews()`/`walls()`.** The doodles wall was `bleed grid auto gap` — a framed photo+drawing pair reaching the true viewport edge, the owner's report. Two fixes: (1) [`/notes/doodles/`](/notes/doodles/) now says `wide`, the correct word for a framed wall (`bleed` is for paint only). (2) The cause in core: `core/Page/Page.css` gained one rule beside the existing `.page-previews` payback — `.page > .bleed:is(.grid, .flex) { padding-inline: var(--gutter-x); }` — so any hand-built bled wall of boxes gets the gutter back automatically. That one rule also fixed 6 more pages nobody asked about: DesignTool's [taste/corpus](/framework/ext/DesignTool/taste/corpus/), the [cols](/framework/styles/layouts/cols/) and [cols/matrix](/framework/styles/layouts/cols/matrix/) screens, and the [space](/framework/styles/layouts/space/)/[space/hunt](/framework/styles/layouts/space/hunt/) walls — all had children flush against their own wall edge with no gutter at all.

**Framed box at literal viewport x:0, crawled at 400/1280/1920/3440 across `/`, `/framework/`, `/imagine/`, `/notes/`, `/notes/doodles/` plus the 6 sites above: 1 → 0.** The one hit, at every width, was the doodle tile; nothing else on the site had one, and nothing new appeared. No page gained horizontal scroll. `/`, `/framework/`, `/imagine/` carry zero elements the new selector matches — proven live, not just diffed — so they are untouched by design.

**Left as paint / found, not fixed (out of this task's one-rule fence):** four more bled grid/flex walls sit inside `/imagine/`'s columns host (`page-column-prose`, a different context than `.page >`) and stay broken the same way — `imagine/feeds/data/cards/`, `imagine/feeds/data/tree/`, `imagine/design/controls/` (bleed wraps a separate grid child, a different shape again), and the Workbench `Board` example. Deliberately untouched: `core/Page/overview/columns/examples/grids/flush-wall/` and `examples/looks/padding/`, which demonstrate the flush-vs-padded choice on purpose — confirmed 0px change. No `flush`/`edge` opt-out word exists yet in framework.css or css-scopes.txt (grepped both); none was invented.
